headline: US Immigration and Customs Enforcement is buying sensor-equipped robot dogs from Connecticut company Radeco in a contract worth 1.3 million dollars.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a government purchase with civil-liberties interest, but the robots are not yet reported in use and the stated purpose is inspection.
importance_line: It puts robot dogs into immigration enforcement, which affects people in communities where ICE operates and raises privacy questions, though DHS describes inspection of dangerous places and the article does not say how the robots will be used day to day.
summary: CT Insider reports that the Department of Homeland Security posted a 1.3 million dollar contract for an Immigration and Customs Enforcement office in Orlando, Florida, with Radeco, a Plainfield, Connecticut, company that fits thermal, infrared and other sensors and software to four-legged robots such as Boston Dynamics' Spot. DHS says the robots would help staff inspect and assess hazards in unsafe, confined or hard-to-reach places, and the sensors include oxygen monitors for tunnels agents discover; Boston Dynamics says it will not sell robots for uses that break privacy and civil rights laws or that carry weapons.
notes: Read from the pre-fetched full text; page dated 10 Oct 2026. machine_action false: a purchase, the robots are not yet reported in use. The posting date of the contract is not stated. The photo caption gives five robots.
